question: What is the primary purpose of decontamination in a clinical setting?

options.A: To remove visible dirt and improve the aesthetic appearance of equipment
options.B: To remove or destroy pathogens and prevent infection transmission
options.C: To extend the physical lifespan of delicate metallic instruments
options.D: To neutralize toxic chemical waste produced during surgery

explanation: Decontamination specifically targets microorganisms to stop the spread of infection to patients and staff. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h1)

question: Why is proper decontamination critical in under-resourced healthcare facilities?

options.A: It shortens the recovery time of patients admitted with severe sepsis
options.B: It compensates for a lack of running water by using chemical sprays
options.C: It prevents hospitals from becoming reservoirs for resistant pathogens
options.D: It eliminates the need for purchasing any disposable medical supplies

explanation: Resource-limited settings often face high infection burdens, making rigorous decontamination vital to stop cross-contamination. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h1)

question: Which processing method destroys all forms of microbial life, including bacterial spores?
explanation: Only sterilization achieves the complete destruction of every microbial form, including resilient spores. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h2)

question: Why must thorough cleaning always be performed before disinfection or sterilization?

options.A: Detergents lower the weight of the instruments for easier autoclaving
options.B: Organic debris can protect and shield microorganisms from chemical agents
options.C: Dry blood makes metallic surfaces completely immune to rust
options.D: Cleaning agents instantly sterilize the instruments on contact

explanation: Blood, protein, and bodily fluids act as a physical barrier that prevents disinfectants and heat from reaching underlying pathogens. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h2)

question: Which Spaulding classification requires absolute sterilization before patient use?
explanation: Critical items enter sterile body cavities and the vascular system, necessitating complete sterilization. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h3)

question: A nurse is preparing a vaginal speculum for reuse on another patient. According to the Spaulding classification, this item is classified as:
explanation: Vaginal specula touch mucous membranes without penetrating sterile tissue, placing them in the semi-critical category. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h3)

question: What is the very first step that should be taken with surgical instruments immediately after a procedure is completed?

options.A: Immediate high-pressure steam sterilization in the operating room
options.B: Point-of-use removal of gross soil and keeping them moist
options.C: Submerging the instruments in concentrated bleach for 24 hours
options.D: Packaging the items tightly in cloth wrappers for transport

explanation: Wiping off heavy contamination and preventing blood from drying makes subsequent cleaning much more effective. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h4)

question: Why is thorough drying of instruments mandated before they undergo sterilization or chemical disinfection?

options.A: Moisture completely blocks the entry of air into the device
options.B: Wet metal surfaces attract airborne fungal spores rapidly
options.C: Water residue can dilute chemical agents and cause instrument corrosion
options.D: Water increases the electrical conductivity of the packaging

explanation: Residual moisture dilutes liquid disinfectants and promotes rust on metal surfaces during heat sterilization. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h4)

question: Why must chlorine-based disinfectant solutions be prepared fresh on a daily basis?

options.A: Fresh mixtures are required by hospital policy to change color
options.B: Microbes develop immediate resistance to older chlorine mixtures
options.C: Chlorine gas evaporates and the solution loses potency over time
options.D: Old chlorine solutions turn into dangerous acids that dissolve plastic buckets

explanation: Active chlorine dissipates quickly when exposed to air and light, making aged solutions unreliable for disinfection. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h5)

question: Which factor most significantly reduces the effectiveness of alcohol-based disinfectants on skin or surfaces?

options.A: Exposure to bright fluorescent overhead hospital lighting
options.B: Dilution with sterile normal saline instead of distilled water
options.C: Presence of visible organic matter like blood or dirt
options.D: Application using non-woven gauze instead of cotton balls

explanation: Organic material inactivates alcohol and blocks direct contact with microorganisms, underscoring the need for prior cleaning. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h5)

question: What type of gloves should a nurse wear when manually washing contaminated surgical instruments?
explanation: Heavy-duty utility gloves provide necessary puncture and chemical resistance during aggressive instrument scrubbing. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a recommended safety feature in a dedicated instrument decontamination room?

options.A: Proper mechanical ventilation and exhaust systems
options.B: Open food and beverage storage refrigerators
options.D: Clearly marked personal protective equipment stations

explanation: Consuming food or storing consumables in a decontamination area creates severe biological contamination risks. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h6)

question: In standard hospital waste management, which color container is typically designated for sharp objects like needles?
explanation: Sharps must be discarded into rigid, puncture-resistant containers to prevent accidental needle-stick injuries. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h7)

question: A patient's blood spills onto the tiled floor of a ward. What is the correct initial action the nurse should take before applying disinfectant?

options.A: Leave the wet spill uncovered to air-dry completely overnight
options.B: Sweep the liquid across the floor into the nearest drainage outlet
options.C: Flood the entire room with water using a high-pressure hose
options.D: Confine the spill and absorb it with disposable paper towels

explanation: Spills must first be absorbed and cleaned of organic matter before chemical disinfection can be effective. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h7)
